risks.risk: Wrong item/capacity: the photo includes multiple tank types (cylindrical black tank and an IBC cube tank), but the listing text doesn’t specify which one you will receive.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the exact tank being sold with a clear view of its capacity marking (litres) and a close-up of the lid/cap and spigot/tap (if any).
risks.if_unproven: Price as the less certain match (worst case: treat as a generic used plastic tank without verified food-grade or leak-proof confirmation).

risks.risk: Leak/crack not visible from this angle: hairline cracks, seam damage, or warped lid sealing can’t be confirmed remotely.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video clip showing the tank filled (or a pressure/soak test) and a close-up of the base and lid area while water is present.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed leak-free (worst case: assume it may need resealing/repair).

risks.risk: Food-grade claim may be unverified: tanks used for other liquids can still look clean.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of any label/stamp indicating food-grade/NSF or the original material certification, plus a close-up of the interior surface.

proof_requests: Confirm which exact tank is for sale (cylindrical black tank vs IBC cube tank) and provide capacity in litres with a readable marking.
Send close-up photos of the lid/cap sealing area and the tank base/seams.
Send a short video showing the tank filled with water (or a leak test) and no dripping around the lid/spigot/base.
response.reason: The photo shows multiple different tank types and the capacity/identity isn’t readable, so a worst-case price cannot be confidently matched to the correct item. Also, food-grade and leak-free claims need direct proof.
